request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user a "Watched due" figure: the due-totals of everyone they watch, added up, or 0.00 when they watch no one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

It was a front-end change only, in `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`; the server and stored data didn't need touching. The header already works out each person's due-total and already loads the sheet's watches. The new figure is in `data-testid="watched-due-total"` and keeps only the watches belonging to the signed-in user. It adds up their due-totals the same way the existing crew total does, skipping anyone whose due-total is n/a.

Because the figure is computed on screen from data the app already fetches, it always matches the due-totals shown elsewhere.
